title: Chicken Cacciatore (White)
subtitle: Italian braised chicken with white wine and herbs
excerpt: Chicken thighs slow-braised in white wine with garlic, rosemary and olives. The sauce stays pale and clean. This is the northern Italian version, lighter than the tomato kind.
sourceNotes: Northern Italian hunter's-style braise, white wine variation common in Lombardy and Veneto.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the braising liquid. Defrost overnight and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily in a large casserole. The sauce improves on the second day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook a day ahead and reheat slowly. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: This is a pale, wine-forward braise without tomatoes. The chicken turns tender and the sauce stays silky from the collagen in the thighs. Keep the heat low once the wine is in or the sauce will reduce too fast.
Season the chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat the olive oil in the large pan over a medium-high heat. Brown the thighs skin-side down for 6 minutes. Turn and brown for 3 minutes more. Set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the same pan and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and rosemary. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up any brown bits from the base. Let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the stock and return the chicken, skin-side up. The liquid should come halfway up the thighs.
Cover and simmer on a low heat for 35 minutes. Uncover and add the olives and capers.
Simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes. Scatter over the parsley and serve.

items.cause: The lid was on during the final simmer.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer for a further 5 to 10 minutes until the sauce reduces.

items.symptom: The chicken skin is pale and soft.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough during browning.
items.fix: This is cosmetic only. The flavour is unaffected. Blast under a hot grill for 3 minutes to crisp the skin.

items.cause: The wine was very acidic and did not cook off fully.
items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar and simmer for 2 more minutes. Taste again before adjusting.
